title: LEFT + FIND: pull out a prefix

screens.prompt: In B6, extract the three-letter prefix from the reference in B2 (everything before the first dash).

hints.syntax: =LEFT(B2,FIND("-",B2)-1) — FIND locates the dash, LEFT takes everything before it.
hints.func-left: LEFT takes the characters from the start of the text; it needs to know how many.
hints.func-find: FIND tells you where the dash is, so LEFT does not have to hard-code the length of the prefix.
hints.require-ref: Read the reference from B2 instead of typing the text into the formula.
hints.value: Close — the off-by-one is the usual culprit. FIND("-",B2) returns 4, the dash itself, so LEFT needs 3 characters, not 4.
hints.error: #VALUE! means FIND could not see the dash at all: check the cell reference and that the dash is in quotes. #NAME? means a function name is misspelled — LEFT needs no dot, no space.

reject.why: off by one: keeps the dash
off by one the other way: OR instead of ORD

docs.explain: The reference in B2 is ORD-2024-0917. FIND("-",B2) scans from the left and returns 4, the position of the first dash — the count starts at 1, not 0. That 4 is one more than the prefix is long, because the dash is not part of the prefix, so the formula subtracts 1 and LEFT takes the first 3 characters: O, R and D, giving "ORD". The result is text, which is why it strings fine next to other text and why it will not match the number 3 without care. The pattern generalises to any delimiter and any prefix length, which is the point: LEFT(B2,3) would have worked today and silently broken on INV-2024-0612, where the prefix also happens to be three letters but the numbers are not always so kind.

errors.text: FIND did not find the dash at all — it raises #VALUE! rather than returning 0.
LEFT(B2,FIND("-",B2)) returns "ORD-" with the dash still attached.
A negative length, which happens when the delimiter is the very first character and the subtraction reaches 0.

docs.atWork: Reference ids, ticket keys, SKU families: anywhere a code carries meaning in its prefix, this pair pulls it out without a helper column and without hard-coded positions.
docs.outcome: Split a reference into parts with LEFT and FIND.
